historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that is one of the two major Sanskrit epics, the other being the Ramayana. It narrates the story of the Kurukshetra War between the Pandava and Kaurava princes. The central character is Krishna, who acts as a mentor, leader and warrior for the Pandava brothers. This epic is estimated to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE.

Another significant reference to Krishna can be found in the Bhagavad Gita, a 700-verse Hindu scripture that is part of the Indian epic Mahabharata. Krishna speaks to the warrior Arjuna about the nature of the universe, duty, and righteousness. This text is estimated to have been written between the 2nd century BCE and the 4th century CE, and is considered a foundational text in Hindu philosophy.
